summary: The maintained installed checker distinguishes whole restored archive SHA512 from NuGet compressed unsigned-content SHA512. It checks the cache sidecar against whole archive bytes, and joins .nupkg.metadata contentHash and the exact lock to package_content_hash. For a signed public package, that data-only projection follows pinned SDK10.0.401/NuGet7.9.0 source: remove the signature physical span and central-directory entry, relocate surviving offsets, adjust EOCD and hash the original compressed bytes. Repacking or hashing decompressed members is not this identity. Unsupported ZIP64, multidisk, encryption, duplicate/path/layout ambiguity refuses. Hash agreement does not verify signature trust or establish installed acceptance: the public path separately requires genuine repository-signature verification, an exact metadata feed source, byte stability, and every retained original payload/Worker member; org retains literal original archive identity. Existing source controls cover signed/unsigned hash roles, signature position, descriptors, malformed layouts and cache/member/source substitution. This is a reusable source contract and algorithm lesson, not a new publication or successful installation claim.
title: Signed NuGet archive identity differs from compressed unsigned content identity
